answer: Sybil resistance rests on a paid identity staked per agent. An identity must lock a real deposit before it speaks, and that deposit is slashed if the same work trace reappears under another key. A thousand clones therefore mean funding a thousand deposits at full price, so attack cost scales linearly with cluster size while each clone earns a fixed yield. Peers weight attestations by stake and age, so a growing trellis of trust lifts honest newcomers while an anonymous meadow of new keys stays near zero. Reward caps and one forge certifying work make splitting identities unprofitable.
